title: Netty's socket buffers live outside the heap, so -Xmx does not bound them
subtitle: Netty pools these buffers instead of reallocating them, and GC never reclaims the pool, so a one-way rise in direct memory is often normal retention rather than a leak.

nodes.label: Direct memory (off-heap)
nodes.detail: Netty socket I/O buffers, pooled by PooledByteBufAllocator

nodes.label: Because direct buffers are native, a WebFlux process can exceed its container limit while the heap still looks healthy.
